synopsis: ISO 34505 was published in June 2025 and provides methods for evaluating and prioritizing test cases, including frequency, criticality, complexity, operational-domain coverage and optimization of test sets [f7181, f4069, f4070]. Its required test-case attributes are identifiers, objectives, inputs, steps, test platform and expected results; the scenario catalog uses the functional, logical and concrete levels adopted from PEGASUS into ISO 34501–34505 [f6732, f6735, f13258]. Across chapters, the standards’ process and information structure are considered transferable to off-road validation, but their content addresses road vehicles and Level 3 and higher automated driving, not off-road compliance [f6642, f7182, f15320]. Off-road adequacy remains unestablished, including validity for mines, quarries, deformable surfaces, articulation, dust and heavy-machinery vibration or contamination [f6734, f7696]. Although ISO 34505 includes a simulation-validity clause, the corpus characterizes these scenario standards as addressing coverage rather than model credibility, without validation against physical data, risk scaling or a prescribed physical-to-virtual testing ratio [f4071, f7693, f8120, f8119, f7694]. ISO 34505 test-case evaluation contributes to the rationale for separating discovery, population-success estimation and requirement/regression campaigns by purpose, data and governance, while that standards evidence remains on-road [f6934, f6666, f6667, f6668].
